newsitem.title: UK: Zinc market eyes falling stocks, Chinese output.
newsitem.headline: Zinc market eyes falling stocks, Chinese output.

text.p: The zinc market is keeping a close eye on zinc stocks for signs that recent falls will reverse and on prospects for higher Chinese output, analysts said in recent reports.
LME inventories were expected to rise sharply after Japanese GSP imports were concluded more than a month ago, but have continued to decline, broker GNI said in a report.
This has caused the broker -- which is not as bullish on zinc as other players -- to review its position, it said in its latest Commodity Perspective.
"We are more than a little nervous about our stance," it said.
"To date there have been two significant stock builds, the first on April 7 of 5,000 tonnes was depleted as quickly as it appeared," GNI said.
The second, of 2,775 tonnes, occurred last Friday. Stocks have continued to decline, and were down 1,025 tonnes on Wednesday to 432,750 tonnes, a fall of 14.4 percent so far in 1997.
"Time will tell whether a new trend has started, but a sudden build could send prices down to $1,200," it added.
Three month prices finished the afternoon LME kerb at $1,273 per tonne on Wednesday afternoon after hitting $1,311 on April 2, the highest so far in 1997.
GNI said its analysis of the supply/demand fundamentals had led it to expect an expansion of mined output, primarily due to high prices.
"Refined metal stocks should be more than ample to meet any projected supply shortfall," it said.
Broker Merrill Lynch said in its latest Commodity Market Trends report that Chinese production would be key to zinc's outlook.
Metals analyst Ted Arnold referred to reports that Chinese producers are seeking to expand exports to 400,000 tonnes this year from the previous 300,000.

"An extra 100,000 tonnes of exports by the Chinese won't stop the bull market in zinc from occurring. But it will certainly blunt the height of the price spikes and the absolute level of the average price," he said.
